notes:
circuit_930 - a three-rail ladder. Top rail y~350-370 (x 110..880), middle rail y~515-540 (x 44..940), bottom rail y~620-640 (x 110..845). Five vertical columns at x~110, 325, 528, 715, 855 tie the rails together, each column carrying a diode or zener between top-and-middle and another between middle-and-bottom. Series elements sit in the rails: 5uH and 15uF in the top rail, 9uF and 4uH in the middle rail, 1uF and 1uH in the bottom rail. Component #13 at (44,538) is a GND symbol drawn rotated 90deg (three shrinking vertical bars) hanging off the LEFT end of the middle rail, so the left segment of the middle rail is net 0; #14 is the conventional GND under the 2k resistor at the far right.

NET MAP (9 nets, 19 components):
  0  = ground. Two disjoint drawn regions that are electrically the same net by definition: (a) the left segment of the middle rail, x 44..~386, carrying GND#13, the V-AC bottom (6.1), the I-DC top (17.0), the zener#5 bottom (5.0), the diode#15 top (15.0) and the 9uF left plate (10.1); (b) the stub under the 2k resistor, R#8 bottom (8.1) into GND#14.
  n3 = top-left corner: V-AC top (6.0) -> up x=113 -> top rail -> left lead of the 5uH inductor (146,354).
  n1 = top rail between the 5uH and the 15uF, x ~232..603: inductor#1 right (1.1), zener#5 top (5.1) at site S0, diode#4 top (4.1) at site S1, 15uF left plate (0.0).
  n2 = top rail right of the 15uF, x ~651..880: 15uF right plate (0.1), zener#3 top (3.1) at site S2, diode#2 top (2.1).
  n5 = centre segment of the middle rail, x ~424..752: 9uF right plate (10.0), diode#4 bottom (4.0) and zener#12 top (12.0) at site S20, zener#3 bottom (3.0) and diode#11 top (11.1) at site S14, 4uH left lead (7.0).
  n4 = right segment of the middle rail, x ~820..940: 4uH right lead (7.1), diode#2 bottom (2.0) and diode#9 top (9.1) at site S15, 2k resistor top (8.0).
  n8 = bottom-left: I-DC bottom (17.1) -> down x=103 -> bottom rail corner -> left plate of the 1uF capacitor (159,642).
  n7 = bottom rail between the 1uF and the 1uH, x ~200..556: 1uF right plate (18.0), diode#15 bottom (15.1) at site S41, zener#12 bottom (12.1) at site S40, 1uH left lead (7.0 -> 16.0).
  n6 = bottom rail right of the 1uH, x ~638..845: 1uH right lead (16.1), diode#11 bottom (11.0) at site S38, diode#9 bottom (9.0).

CRITICAL SITE DECISIONS (all eleven read as JUNCTION):
  S0 (332,356), S1 (532,368), S2 (730,373) - deg=3 plain T's where a column's upper lead meets the top rail. Nothing to pass through; reading anything else would strand the zener#5 / diode#4 / zener#3 anodes on one-terminal nets. JUNCTION.
  S14 (712,518), S15 (848,517), S18 (107,531), S19 (319,532), S20 (523,534) - deg=4 crossings of a column through the middle rail. Every one of these carries a clearly drawn filled SOLDER DOT: the crops show a symmetric black blob about 3x the stroke width in both axes centred exactly on the intersection (dot scores 2.2-2.7, versus 1.0-1.6 for every non-dotted site on this sheet). The reported hop scores of 1.4-5.7 come from the rails being drawn freehand and sagging slightly at each column, not from a drawn hop or jog - there is no semicircular arc anywhere. JUNCTION. Had these been read as crossings, each column would become a floating two-diode series string with no connection to its rail, and the 9uF / 4uH middle-rail sections would carry no branch at all - a disconnected island in every case.
  S38 (708,620), S41 (322,634) - deg=3 plain T's where a column's lower lead meets the bottom rail. JUNCTION.
  S40 (523,627) - reported deg=4 hop=3.6, but the crop shows a plain T: the zener#12 bottom lead comes down and stops on the bottom rail. The extra branch and the hop score are the zener's own bent cathode bar ink at (505..545, 600..615) sitting just above the rail, not a wire that continues below. JUNCTION; a crossing would strand the zener's cathode.

PORT FIXES (three terminals had landed on handwritten value-label ink, each producing a one-terminal net):
  #1 Inductor (5uH) t0: was p1 @(184,377), a stroke of the '5uH' label written under the coil. Moved to p4 @(146,354), the real left lead. This merged the old singleton n3 with the old singleton n6 (V-AC top) - they are the same wire run (both wire_len 82).
  #10 Capacitor (9uF) t1: was p2 @(390,564), a stroke of the '9uF' label. Moved to p1 @(386,534), the real left plate lead, which runs left along the middle rail to GND#13 - so this terminal is net 0.
  #17 I-DC (3A) t1: was p2 @(130,593), a stroke of the '3A' text. Moved to p3 @(103,615), the real bottom lead. This merged old singletons n10 and n11 (the 1uF capacitor's left plate, same wire run, wire_len 91).
After these three fixes every net has at least two terminals.

CLASS CHECK: I zoomed component #9 @(844,565) at 14x because its cathode bar has a downward tick on the left end and at first glance resembles the zeners. It is NOT a zener: the true zeners on this sheet (#3, #5, #12) all have a bar bent at BOTH ends into a clear 'Z', while #9's bar is straight with a single short pen tick on the left end - exactly the same tick the drafter puts on the unambiguous plain diode #15 @(322,596). #9 = Diode is correct as annotated. All other classes match the drawn symbols (V-AC = circle with sine, I-DC = circle with arrow, both GNDs verified including the rotated one at the far left). No 3-terminal parts, so no pin-order questions.
